header.title: From full disk to *a clear decision.*
header.lede: Follow the folder tree, inspect developer storage, and keep every cleanup behind a separate review.

items.title: Follow *the space.*
items.body: Browse live scan results, folder graphs and the inspector. Developer Insights highlights caches, build outputs, packages, node_modules, .git and AI storage. Save snapshots to compare later scans.

detail.alt: StorageDaddy treemap of a sample folder: Projects, Builds, Caches, AI Sessions, Packages and Documents sized by space on disk

items.title: See your *AI footprint.*
items.body: Inspect recognized local Claude and Codex histories, skills and project context. Context-load estimates are not measurements of an agent’s entire runtime context. Selected session exports are reading archives, not resumable backups.

detail.alt: Illustration of two small characters wheeling a folder full of documents and code files

blocks.title: A scan *deletes nothing.*
blocks.lede: Builds, caches, installed packages and agent histories accumulate quietly. StorageDaddy brings their sizes and locations into one native workspace.

points.title: Inspect first
points.body: Browse scan results, folder graphs and the inspector before choosing anything.

points.title: Review candidates
points.body: Add candidates, then review the list with local evidence and readable paths.

points.title: Confirm separately
points.body: Moving to Trash is its own explicit confirmation. StorageDaddy does not automatically empty Trash.

blocks.eyebrow: Your files stay on your Mac
blocks.title: Local scans. *Explicit cleanup.*
blocks.lede: Scanning, previews and archive validation run locally. The native app has no file uploads or app telemetry. Sparkle checks for updates over HTTPS; installation remains your choice.

blocks.title: For the Mac *you build on.*
blocks.lede: The public beta is signed and notarized for Apple silicon Macs on macOS 14 or later. There is no trial expiry, account or checkout.

points.title: Made for
points.body: Developers who want to understand disk usage and review specific cleanup candidates, with local evidence and readable paths.

points.title: Not for
points.body: Automatic deletion, guaranteed reclaimed-space totals, an Intel build, or a replacement for a backup.

items.a: No. Add candidates, review the list, then explicitly confirm moving them to Trash. StorageDaddy does not automatically empty Trash.

items.q: Why can totals differ from macOS Storage?
items.a: Allocated and logical sizes differ. Shared APFS blocks, snapshots, protected files and scan scope also affect totals. Allocated bytes are not a guarantee of space reclaimed.

items.q: Do I need Full Disk Access?
items.a: It is optional and enables broader coverage. Protected or unreadable locations may still be skipped. A folder scan is a useful starting point.
The current beta is free. Everyone who downloads during early access gets future versions free forever. There is no account, checkout, subscription or trial expiry today.
